scope.levels: All new tasks omit jlpt. Dictionary senses and existing word levels do not classify these complete Grammar tasks.
scope.identityPolicy: No word card, existing exercise object, existing group membership, level, exclusion or scheduling identity changes. New exercise IDs have independent existing Grammar schedules; accepted variants have no separate schedules.

placement.entry: Grammar, All or Unclassified for new material, then the Onomatopoeia in sentences chapter/set and targeted practice. The browser has its own scope: Clear search and browse filters, or Filters and next topic followed by All/Unclassified. Accessible list is an alternative to the diagram. Native Unclassified chapter/group and Article sets entry passed through production components.
placement.reason: A cross-construction thematic chapter with supplied vocabulary. Prerequisite exposure to basic verbs, noun modification and state/change is helpful, but no new unsupplied compound operation justifies a hard gate. Root groups do not imply beginner language or word mastery.
placement.compatibility: Only existing schema-1 exercises, authored groups and the existing curriculum namespace. Older readers can ignore the catalog. Existing partial mappings, unowned compatibility exercises and all old edges remain unchanged.

sources.publisher: Shogakukan, Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten via Kotobank
sources.evidence: Separates bowing, flexing/denting and hunger. Hunger has adjectival-noun use, but [1]3 also records historical 腹がペコペコして.
sources.limits: Do not teach an absolute hunger-plus-する ban. The pilot uses ordinary hunger state/change frames and rejects options only in the actual printed frame.

sources.section: わくわく, 副(スル), definition and first example
sources.evidence: Excited expectation; the example explicitly permits と before the causative させる. The historical worry qualification is retained as outside the selected modern eager-anticipation use.

sources.section: どきどき, 副(スル), definition and examples
sources.evidence: Pounding heartbeat from exertion or emotion; both exertion and anticipation/anxiety examples use する. Positive excitement is not compulsory.

sources.section: にこにこ, 副(スル), definition and examples
sources.evidence: Explicit にこにこ(と)笑う and にこにこして話しかける. A visible friendly smile need not be laughter aloud or proof of sincerity.

sources.publisher: Shogakukan, Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten via Kotobank
sources.section: First きらきら entry, [1]1 and [2]
sources.evidence: Glittering light, often with と; separate historical adjectival and laughter entries exist.
sources.limits: Do not turn the preferred adverbial model into a universal に ban. Avoid unrelated song/fish names and historical laughter when reviewing this light sense.

sources.evidence: The teaching discussion supplies an everyday に versus written/formal と register distinction, but its broad na-adjective restriction is not adopted as an exceptionless rule. Contemporary edited event prose attests へとへととなった; hiking and travel accounts attest hunger-sense ペコペコとなった. These corroborate the selected alternatives rather than transfer bowing or denting into hunger.
sources.limits: Exact usage attestations are not a frequency survey. The guide retains に as the everyday state-change model; no equal-frequency or unrestricted suffix-product claim.

sources.evidence: Footwear-fit とする, fluffy bread/texture する noun descriptions, and exertion-related heartbeat とする were checked separately against actual same-sense passages. The ている explanation supports ordinary てる contraction.
sources.limits: Product reviews and private blogs are corroborating usage, not independent grammar authorities or comparative-frequency evidence. The clinical page is used only for language attestation, not medical advice.

wordConstructionMatrix.restriction: Retain the supplied sleep verb; no universal する or な model.
The final と is part of the supplied word; do not add another と. Emphatic lengthening and the separate しておく idiom are not elicited.
Light reflected by frost or moving costume; retain the supplied light verb, not figurative brilliance or historical laughter.
The supplied 笑う describes smiling; no required audible laugh.
Keep physical security and dependable character distinct. Descriptive した does not mean the person has ceased to be dependable.
Suru transformations and supplied ongoing-state frames. Do not infer optional と from the unrelated volitional とする.
Fear and physical exertion, not invariably excitement; no diagnosis.
The subject experiences irritation; this is not deliberately irritating another person.
Ordinary present-characteristic modifiers; include fitting の/な and verbal variants, not a single mandatory suffix. Floating/illness senses and headline compounds are not elicited.
Wearer-relative fit, not softness, historical floating, horn sound or yielding ground. Do not reject fitting の/な/した alternatives.
Current exhaustion versus becoming exhausted; no universal ban inferred from missing source examples.
Hunger frames only, not bowing or a flexible surface; historical hunger する is explicitly not declared impossible.

answerPolicy.word: Keep the supplied kana word, permitting hiragana or katakana but not different emphatic word shapes or added content words.
answerPolicy.blank: Always include the mimetic word in the blank; optional omission of a connector never requires empty input.
answerPolicy.variants: Enumerate full accepted strings, including supported short してる forms where ongoing modifiers are permitted. NFKC is not kana folding. An accepted alternative is not automatically a separate construction target.
answerPolicy.options: Evaluate each whole completion. Wrong attachments in this frame do not prove a word/construction impossible elsewhere. Additional correct choices are choose-any and appear only occasionally.
answerPolicy.nounModifiers: Sentence modifiers describing the selected present characteristic, not product labels/headlines, added similes, past-only states or arbitrarily extended clauses. A clearly named した transformation is the one narrower noun-modifier drill.
answerPolicy.reviewGate: The independent initial review read all 44 complete tasks, 262 accepted-string occurrences, 153 option rationales and the full guide. It returned CLEAN on correctness, scoped coverage and comprehensibility, with no actionable findings. Vocabulary/delta reconciliation and native acceptance are recorded separately.

contextPolicy: Exercise IDs below use the onoma- prefix. Introduction member exampleKeys are the final context mapping. Paired interpretation claims share one key; related texture/contact, oversized-footwear, exertion-change and hunger-change repetitions share keys even when noun/background wording changes. Counts are not independent mastery or transfer counts.
